newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria's new international debt fund takes off.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria's new international debt fund takes off.

text.p: Investors were upbeat when application lists for a new instrument to trade Nigeria's internationally quoted debts on the local stock market opened on Monday, traders said.

The Nigeria International Debt Fund aims to trade up to $100 million and the promoters said the private-sector initiated instrument would pool together capital of investors keen on the governments dollar-denominated par bonds and promissory notes.

"Investors mostly interested are institutional investors who know they are going to be able to make payments in dollars in future, say for machinery," Phillip Ihenacho of U.K.-based Afrinvest Securities Ltd., told brokers at a presentation.

"It is also about protecting your purchasing power in dollar terms," he said, adding initial interest in the instrument was so high that some brokers were worried whether it had not been pre-sold already.
"Some institutional investors have shown interest but the fund has not been pre-sold," he told Reuters.
Investors will be able to buy a minimum of $5,000 but it will trade in units of $1,000 at the secondary market after application lists close on March 14.
A senior official of the Nigerian stock exchange said it was the first financial derivative in the market and it showed the Nigerian market was getting more sophisticated.
The promoters expect the investment to yield not less than eight percent, which they said was higher than U.S. money market rates.

The fund was developed over the last year and involves the local subsidiary of America's Citibank, Nigerian International Bank (NIB) and United Bank for Africa (UBA), one of the countrys top three banks.
